items.text: Group schemes over a field are separated
Recall: a group scheme over a field is separable iff normal iff has one separable point; if locally of finite type, iff smooth; then irreducible components = connected components.
A rational point of a scheme over $k$ is closed (a section over $\operatorname{Spec}k$).
Proposition. $G$ a group scheme over any base $S$: $G$ is separated iff the unit section is a closed immersion.
\Delta_G=(g,h\mapsto gh^{-1})^{-1}(e)\ \subset G\times G
The composition law is open
\alpha\colon G\times G\to G\times G,\ (g,x)\mapsto(gx,x)\ \text{(isomorphism)},\qquad \pi=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\alpha
$\mathrm{pr}_1$ is open (universally open over a field), so $\pi$ is open.

More generally $G$ acting on $X$: $\pi\colon G\times X\to X$ is $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\alpha_X$, $\alpha_X(g,x)=(gx,x)$; if $\alpha_X$ is an isomorphism ($X$ a pseudo-torsor), $\pi$ is open and faithfully flat.
Products of subsets $UV$
$U\subset G$, $V\subset X$ open; $UV=\pi(U\times V)$. Let $G^0$ be the irreducible component of the identity.
(a) $\pi$ open $\Rightarrow$ $UV$ open.
(b) $UV$ is stable under $G^0$.
(c) ($X$ a pseudo-torsor, or $G$ itself) $UV$ is stable under specialisation.
(d) ($U,V$ quasi-compact, or $G$ locally of finite type) $UV$ is closed.

Corollary: $X$ is covered by open and closed quasi-compact subsets $U\cdot X_i$; hence the connected components of $X$ are quasi-compact, and (every point lies on only one irreducible component) irreducible = connected components; in particular the neutral component is $G^0$.
(d) follows from (c): a retrocompact open set stable under specialisation is closed ($X$ separated).
Proof of (b)
Base change so that $x=u_0v_0$ with $u_0\in U(k)$, $v_0\in V(k)$, and $g\in G^0(k)$. Need $u\in U$, $v\in V$ with $gx=uv$.
\varphi\colon G\to X,\ \varphi(h)=h\cdot x;\qquad gx=uv\iff u^{-1}gx=v\iff u\in g\,\varphi^{-1}(V)^{-1}
T=G^0u_0\ \text{closed irreducible};\quad U\cap T\ni u_0,\qquad g\varphi^{-1}(V)^{-1}\cap T\ni gu_0\quad(\text{since }\varphi(u_0^{-1})=u_0^{-1}u_0v_0=v_0\in V)
Two non-empty opens of the irreducible $T$ meet: $UV$ is stable under $G^0$, for any $G$-space $X$.
Proof of (c)
Lemma. $X$ a pseudo-torsor, $W\subset X$ any subset: $W$ is stable under $G^0$ iff $W$ is stable under specialisation and generalisation. (Stability of $UV$ under generalisation holds as it is open.)

Proof. Pass to $k'$ with $x\in W$ rational; generalisations lift by flatness. $\varphi_x\colon G\to X$ is generalising (isomorphism for a torsor), $G^0$ stable under generalisation, $\varphi_x(1)=x$, so the image of $G^0$ contains $y$.
Homogeneous spaces

$X$ is a homogeneous space under $G$: $X\ne\varnothing$ and, for a point $x$ (after extension), $\varphi_x\colon G\to X$ is an epimorphism (fpqc), so $X=G/G_x$; for our purpose: $X\ne\varnothing$ and $\varphi_x$ surjective.

$\varphi_x$ surjective $\Rightarrow$ universally generalising: a maximal point $z$ of $X$ has non-empty fibre; reduce to $k$ perfect, $G$ and $X$ reduced; $G\to X$ is flat at the points above $z$ (the local ring is a field), hence everywhere by translation; flat $\Rightarrow$ universally generalising.
Lemma
$f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes with $G$-action (compatible), $G$ acting transitively set-theoretically on $X$. Equivalent:

(a) $f$ is generalising at some point of $X$; (b) $f$ is universally generalising; (c) some maximal point of $Y$ has non-empty fibre; (d) for an irreducible component $X^0$ of $X$, $f(X^0)$ is an irreducible component of $Y$.

(a)$\Rightarrow$(c): a maximal generalisation $y'$ of $f(x)$ has a point of $X$ above it. (c)$\Rightarrow$(b): reduce to $k$ perfect, reduced; flat at one point, hence at all by translation. (d)$\Rightarrow$(c): the generic point of $f(X^0)$ is maximal.
(c)$\Rightarrow$(d): $X^0$ is stable under specialisation and generalisation, hence under $G^0$ (lemma).
